research_rationale: EO 10457 (18 FR 3083, signed 1953-05-27) designates the Department of Justice as a defense agency of the United States for the purposes of chapter 17 of title 35, United States Code (patent secrecy). I read the held Federal Register original in full (jobs/fr-originals/data/full_run/texts/EO_10457.txt, characters 1606-3140): its number, title, date, signature line and filing line (F.R. Doc. 53-4777) agree, and the page text above it belongs to the preceding order, EO 10456, so the inventory span starts at the EO 10457 heading. The order has one operative clause, the designation in its final paragraph. It has no expiry date, condition, reporting duty, delegation or revocation. For the current predicate I used the original-plus-bounded-search route: the held original, no held later instrument attached because none was found, no own-terms end, and the three bounded machine searches (current-law:usc, current-law:ecfr, later-events:ofr_catalog) after reading their coverage statements. The U.S. Code search covers the release point current through 2026-10-09 and does not reflect laws enacted from 2026-10-10 through 2026-10-14; the eCFR search is point-in-time as of 2026-10-14; the catalog search covers 6942 catalog records. The current-law:usc search found one hit for this order, a note under 35 U.S.C. 188 that records the Department of Justice designation by this order (the jobs/current-law/output/MENTIONS.csv row for the order); that note text is not held as bytes, so it is context for the search result and not a cited source. The order recites the statute it implements, section 181 of title 35, which provides for designation of an agency by the President as a defense agency. No held source shows that section or chapter 17 repealed or expired. No held instrument amends, revokes or supersedes EO 10457: the OFR disposition table in jobs/peano-formulario lists no amending, revoking or superseding order for it, and the held-text number search lists only the Federal Register page that prints it and the 1989 OFR Codification, which prints it as in force on 1989-01-20.
savings_reason: The order has no savings, transition or residual-effects clause, and the claim does not assert that it ended. Nothing remains to be saved: the single designation continues to operate under the same terms.
earlier_end_check: Searched for any earlier end. The order has no own-terms end (no date, condition, deadline or reporting clause). The held-text number search (LOOKUPS.md) returns only the issue page that prints EO 10456 and EO 10457 together and the 1989 OFR Codification; neither revokes or supersedes it. The OFR disposition table lists no amendment, revocation or supersession. The later-events:ofr_catalog search found 0 hits.
scope_check: The single clause is the whole order, so there is no partial revocation or amendment to separate from it. The designation is for the purposes of chapter 17 of title 35 only, and the claim asserts nothing about any other chapter.
independent_command_check: There is only one command, the designation of the Department of Justice as a defense agency. The recitals describe section 181 of the patent statute and give no separate command.
savings_check: No savings clause exists, and no later order is held that could have transferred or saved anything; the claim asserts continuation and records the savings state as none after bounded search.

research_rationale: EO 10521 (19 FR 1499, signed 1954-03-17) sets out how Federal agencies administer scientific research and assigns the National Science Foundation policy, study and review duties. I read the held Federal Register original in full (jobs/fr-originals/data/full_run/texts/EO_10521.txt). Its number, title, date, signature and filing line (F.R. Doc. 54-2014) agree. Inventory: the dossier's Section 6 span ran through a printed contents page, so I corrected the inventory to 14 spans of the order's own text (Section 6 appears in two parts around the page break). Later events: EO 10807 (24 FR 1897, signed 1959-03-13), section 6(b)(1)-(4), amended the order: it substituted a new Section 1, inserted the word basic in Section 3, edited the ends of Section 8(a) and (b), revoked Section 8(c), and added a new Section 10. Section 6(c) of EO 10807 says the two orders do not limit each other's agencies' functions. EO 10807 itself was later amended and the Council it created was abolished by statute (the OFR table notes Public Law 94-282), but no held source says that this affected the amendments EO 10807 made to EO 10521. The Office of the Federal Register disposition table (jobs/peano-formulario) also lists EO 12608 (1987-09-09) as amending EO 10521. The held text of EO 12608 does not name EO 10521 or any of its subjects; its Section 2 substitutes Office of Management and Budget for Bureau of the Budget in listed orders and in any other order relating to functions delegated to that Office, and the held EO 10521 original contains no such words, so that provision does not change EO 10521 and is not claimed as a later event. Only Section 8(c) ended; every other original clause is claimed operative on 2026-10-14, so the order is claimed in force. Current predicate: original-plus-bounded-search route; I read the coverage of current-law:usc (release point current through 2026-10-09; later laws to 2026-10-14 not reflected), current-law:ecfr (as of 2026-10-14) and later-events:ofr_catalog before selecting them. No held source shows the order or its amendments revoked, superseded or expired, and the order rests on the President's own authority as recited (no statute that could lapse).
savings_reason: The order contains no savings or transition clause. The only ending is the revocation of Section 8(c) by EO 10807, which carries no savings text in the held order either; nothing in the claim depends on a saved residual effect, and the claim asserts continuation of the rest of the order.
earlier_end_check: Searched for any earlier end of each clause. The order has no own-terms end date or condition; the phrase about reports in Section 9 is a continuing duty, not a deadline. The OFR disposition table and the later-events catalog name only EO 10807 (amendments and the Section 8(c) revocation) and EO 12608 (which does not name this order, see rationale). A held-text number search for the order lists EO 10807, the 1989 OFR Codification, a 2005 Federal Register rule (70 FR 55725) that cites the order as a policy of the National Science Foundation, and the Federal Register original. No earlier end of any other clause was found.
scope_check: EO 10807 revoked only paragraph (c) of Section 8 and changed other provisions by amendment; each amendment is attached to the clause it changes, so the partial revocation is not read as ending the order or any other clause. Under the owner's strike-and-insert ruling of 2026-10-21 an amended clause continues in amended form, with before-and-after text recorded for Sections 1, 3, 8(a) and 8(b).
independent_command_check: Sections 1 to 9 are separate directions to the Foundation and to agency heads. Section 6 (four practices, split by the page break), Section 7 and each paragraph of Section 8 are independent commands; Section 8(c) ended without affecting them.
savings_check: No savings text exists and none is asserted. Section 8(c) was revoked outright, with the committee it relied on revoked in the same order; the claim does not depend on any residual effect of that paragraph.

research_rationale: EO 10579 (19 FR 7925, signed 1954-11-30) prescribes regulations under which the Administrator of General Services establishes, operates, curtails and discontinues interagency motor-vehicle pools and systems. I read the held Federal Register original in full (jobs/fr-originals/data/full_run/texts/EO_10579.txt): the number, title, date, signature and filing line (F.R. Doc. 54-9551) agree. The dossier listed 35 fragments, some inside printed contents-page text, so I replaced them with 12 spans of the order's own text (Section 3 in two parts around the page break). The order has eleven sections with no expiry date; its day counts (thirty-day notice, forty-five-day appeals, seventy-five-day decisions) and the discontinuance conditions are procedures for each study, determination, appeal or pool, not ends of the sections. The dossier's machine own-terms leads on Sections 5, 8(f) and 9 are of that kind. No later instrument is held that amends, revokes or supersedes the order: the OFR disposition table lists none for EO 10579, the later-events catalog search found 0 hits, and the held-text number search lists only the 1989 OFR Codification and the 41 CFR part 101-39 text, which cite it as in use. The dossier lists EO 10578 as a possible acting order, but the held ProQuest replica of EO 10578 shows only the adjacent page of the issue (EO 10578 concerns railroad labor disputes and the replica also prints the heading of EO 10579); it contains no provision amending EO 10579. EO 12608 (1987) section 2 substitutes the Office of Management and Budget for the Bureau of the Budget in orders listed there and in any other order that relates to functions delegated to that Office; it does not name EO 10579, the OFR table does not list it for EO 10579, and the packet holds it as no evidence record, so it is recorded here only as a possible wording change to the references to the Director of the Bureau of the Budget and is not claimed as an ending. Authority: the order cites the Federal Property and Administrative Services Act of 1949 (sections 107, 205(a) and 211(c)) and section 202 of the Budget and Accounting Procedures Act of 1950; those provisions have since been restated in other titles of the U.S. Code and no restated text is held here, so the claim rests on the held current regulations that still cite the order as their governing instrument rather than on the successor statutes' text. Current predicate: original-plus-bounded-search route after reading the coverage of the three searches.
savings_reason: The order has no savings or transition clause. The claim asserts continuation, and the only transfers provided for (Sections 4 and 8(f)) are made case by case when a determination or discontinuance occurs, so no residual effect depends on an ending.
earlier_end_check: Searched for any earlier end. The order has no own-terms end date or end condition. The OFR disposition table lists no amendment, revocation or supersession; the later-events catalog search found 0 hits. The held-text number search finds only the 1989 OFR Codification and 41 CFR part 101-39 text citing the order as in use. EO 10578 does not amend it (the dossier lead is the neighbouring page of the same issue).
scope_check: No partial revocation or amendment of any section is held. The wording point about the Director of the Bureau of the Budget (EO 12608 section 2) is recorded in the rationale as unattached; it would be a name substitution, not an ending.
independent_command_check: Sections 1 to 11 are separate rules: purpose and Administrator's duty, studies, determinations, transfers, effective dates, appeals, compliance, discontinuance, exemptions, optional use and supplementary regulations. The exemptions in Section 9 are a list within one rule. Each is claimed operative on the same basis.
savings_check: No savings clause exists and none is asserted. The claim records the savings state as none after bounded search.

research_rationale: EO 10641 (20 FR 8137, signed 1955-10-26) amends the Civil Service Rules prescribed by EO 10577 by adding Rule VIII, Appointments to Overseas Positions (sections 8.1 to 8.4). I read the held Federal Register original in full (jobs/fr-originals/data/full_run/texts/EO_10641.txt, characters 759-3469 for the order's operative paragraph): the number, title, date, signature line and filing line (F.R. Doc. 55-8799) agree, and the page text after it belongs to EO 10642, which is a different order. The dossier lists one clause, the whole amendment instruction containing Rule VIII, and I kept that inventory: Rule VIII is added as a single instrument and the claim does not separate its four sections. The order has no expiry date. The machine own-terms leads in the dossier are conditions on the Commission's authority in section 8.2 (a shortage-of-registers finding that the Commission makes) and a retirement-act exclusion in the same section; they condition particular appointments and do not end the rule. Later events: EO 12107 (44 FR 1055, signed 1978-12-28, effective 1979-01-01) section 2-101 amends the order by substituting Office of Personnel Management for Civil Service Commission and related titles in the orders listed there, which include EO 10641; its section 2-103 amends Rules II, IV and V of EO 10577 but not Rule VIII; its general effective date is 1979-01-01. The OFR disposition table lists only EO 12107 as amending EO 10641. Two later orders held in the repository refer to Rule VIII without amending it: EO 12362 (1982) section 4 and EO 12721 (1990) section 3 each say that, to the extent of any conflict, the order controls over Civil Service Rule 8.2 (5 CFR 8.2). A precedence-in-conflict rule treats Rule 8.2 as existing and does not revoke or supersede it. Those texts are not evidence records in this packet, so they cannot be cited as later events here; I note them for the reviewer. Current predicate: original-plus-bounded-search route, after reading the coverage of current-law:usc (release point current through 2026-10-09; later laws to 2026-10-14 not reflected), current-law:ecfr (as of 2026-10-14) and later-events:ofr_catalog. The held eCFR text of 5 CFR part 301 (Overseas Employment, jobs/theophilus-sources/output/texts/cfr-t5-part301.txt, GovInfo eCFR bulk amended through 2026) cites E.O. 10577 as amended by E.O. 10641 in its authority line, and its subpart B regulates overseas limited appointments, the subject of section 8.2; that is context from the ecfr search and not a cited source. EO 10577, which prescribes the rules Rule VIII was added to, is not revoked in the OFR table (it lists amendments only), and held EO 13467 (2008) and EO 13764 (2017) each state that nothing in them supersedes EO 10577 as amended.
savings_reason: The order has no savings or transition clause and the claim asserts that Rule VIII continues. The only held later event is a change of agency names. The retirement-act exclusion in section 8.2 is part of the same clause and is not separately claimed as ended or continuing beyond what the clause-level basis supports.
earlier_end_check: Searched for any earlier end. The order has no own-terms end (no date, deadline or termination condition). The OFR disposition table lists only EO 12107 as amending it, and the later-events catalog search reports 2 hits for it, which are the OFR disposition note for the EO 12107 amendment and a see-reference to EO 10577. The held-text number search finds EO 10577 (the parent), a 1995 and a 2025 Federal Register document and 5 CFR text that cite it as authority; none revokes it. EO 12362 and EO 12721 mention Rule 8.2 only in a precedence-in-conflict section and neither revokes or supersedes Rule VIII.
scope_check: The target of the instrument is Rule VIII only. EO 12107 section 2-103 changes Rules II, IV and V of EO 10577 and does not touch Rule VIII, and the title substitution in section 2-101 is a wording amendment, not an ending. A revocation of part of EO 10577 would have to be checked against Rule VIII; the OFR table shows no revocation of any part of EO 10577.
independent_command_check: Rule VIII sections 8.1 to 8.4 are one grant of authority with its conditions and one exclusion; none is a separate dated or conditional command that could have ended on its own, and no held source shows any of them ended.
savings_check: No savings clause exists in the order and no later order is held that saved or transferred anything. The claim records the savings state as none after bounded search.
